memory_chunk_context.description: Expand a chunk with its neighbors from the same source. Given a chunk_id from a prior search, returns the surrounding chunks in timestamp order — showing the full conversation/document context around a match.
memory_chunk_context.name: memory_chunk_context

chunk_id.description: ID of the chunk to retrieve context for (from a prior search result).

window.description: Number of neighboring chunks to include before and after (default 2).

memory_hybrid_search.description: Multi-signal hybrid search with configurable weight profiles. Combines graph relevance, vector similarity, keyword matching, and freshness into a unified score. Choose a mode to emphasize the signal most relevant to your query: 'balanced' (equal graph+vector), 'semantic' (vector-heavy), 'lexical' (keyword-heavy), 'graph_first' (relationship-heavy).
memory_hybrid_search.name: memory_hybrid_search

include_breakdown.description: Show per-signal score breakdown for each result (default false).

memory_store_kinds.description: Return the catalog of memory_store storage kinds the active memory driver persists. No arguments. Use when planning a multi-kind retrieval fan-out.
memory_store_kinds.name: memory_store_kinds

memory_store_raw_chunks.description: List raw memory_store chunks (timestamp DESC) matching structured filters: source kind, source id, owner, time range, required tags. No scoring or rerank — use for exact-subset inspection, not search. Returns full Chunk rows with metadata and content.
memory_store_raw_chunks.name: memory_store_raw_chunks

tags_all_of.description: Post-filter: chunk.metadata.tags must contain every tag listed.

memory_store_raw_search.description: Free-text LIKE search over the canonical entity index. Returns entity ids ranked by total mention count across every tree. Use to discover what entities (people, channels, threads) exist in the memory store before drilling into a tree with the memory_tree_* tools. Pass `kinds` to narrow the result set (e.g. only people).
memory_store_raw_search.name: memory_store_raw_search

kinds.description: Optional entity kind filter (e.g. ["person", "channel"]). Empty/absent = all kinds.

query.description: Substring matched against canonical entity id and surface form (case-insensitive).

memory_tools_list.description: List every stored memory rule for the given tool. Rules are durable learnings about how to use the tool — priorities, gotchas, user edicts. Returns the rules ordered by priority (Critical → Low) and updated_at DESC within each priority.
memory_tools_list.name: memory_tools_list

memory_tools_put.description: Record a durable rule / learning for the given tool. Use when the user gives a directive that should survive future sessions, or when a tool failure pattern is worth pinning. Returns the stored rule with its assigned id and timestamps.
memory_tools_put.name: memory_tools_put

priority.description: How aggressively to surface the rule. Default: normal.

rule.description: Free-text rule, edict, or learning to pin.

tool_name.description: Exact tool name the rule applies to.

memory_tree.description: Query the user's ingested email/chat/document memory tree. Set `mode` to one of: `search_entities` (resolve a name to a canonical id — call first when the user mentions someone by name), `query_source` (filter by source type + time window), `drill_down` (expand a coarse summary one level), `cover_window` (minimum node set covering a time window [since_ms, until_ms] — use for last-24h / time-bounded recaps), `fetch_leaves` (pull raw chunks for citation), `ingest_document` (write a document into the tree for future retrieval), `walk` / `smart_walk` (deterministic E2GraphRAG retrieval — extracts query entities, routes between entity-graph (local) and dense-summary (global) search with no LLM, and returns ranked evidence hits for a natural-language query).
memory_tree.name: memory_tree

body.description: ingest_document: document body (markdown or plain text).

chunk_ids.description: fetch_leaves: list of chunk ids to pull.

kinds.description: search_entities: optional entity kind filter (email, url, handle, person, ...).

max_depth.description: drill_down: how many levels to expand (default 1, max 3).

max_hops.description: walk / smart_walk: entity-graph relatedness hop threshold for E2GraphRAG routing (default 2, capped at 4).

mode.description: Which operation to run (retrieval or write).

node_id.description: drill_down: id of the summary node to expand.

provider.description: ingest_document: source provider (e.g. github, web, root_docs). Defaults to agent.

query.description: search_entities: substring to match. query_source: semantic rerank query (optional). walk: natural-language question to answer by walking the memory tree.

source_id.description: ingest_document / query_source: stable source identifier. For ingest, re-ingesting same id replaces old chunks.

source_kind.description: query_source: source type to filter (chat, email, document, ...).

source_ref.description: ingest_document: optional URL back to original source.

time_window_days.description: query_source / walk / smart_walk: look-back window in days (applied to the dense/global branch for walk).

memory_tree_cover_window.description: Return the MINIMUM set of memory nodes covering a time window [since_ms, until_ms] (epoch-milliseconds): condensed summaries where a whole stretch is in-window, raw recent chunks otherwise. Grouped by source, ordered oldest→newest. Use for time-bounded recaps (e.g. a last-24h morning brief) instead of `query_source` (which is all-time).
memory_tree_cover_window.name: memory_tree_cover_window

source_kind.description: Source kind filter when no exact id is known.

memory_tree_drill_down.description: Walk a summary node's children one step (or more if `max_depth > 1`). Returns leaf chunks for an L1 summary, or lower-level summaries for L2+. Use this when a `query_*` summary is too coarse and you want to expand it. Pass `query` to rerank children by cosine similarity.
memory_tree_drill_down.name: memory_tree_drill_down

limit.description: Optional cap on returned hits, applied after rerank.

max_depth.description: How many levels down to walk (default 1).

node_id.description: Id of the summary (or leaf) to expand.

query.description: Optional natural-language query — when set, children are reranked by cosine similarity.

memory_tree_fetch_leaves.description: Batch-fetch raw chunk rows by id (max 20 per call). Use this when you need verbatim content for a citation — the `content` and `source_ref` fields on each hit are the authoritative quote source.
memory_tree_fetch_leaves.name: memory_tree_fetch_leaves

chunk_ids.description: Chunk ids to hydrate. Capped at 20 per call.

memory_tree_query_source.description: Return summaries from per-source memory trees, optionally filtered by `source_id` (exact), `source_kind` (chat/email/document) and/or `time_window_days`. Use this for intents like "in my email last week..." or "summarise our slack #eng activity". Newest-first by default; pass `query` for semantic rerank.
memory_tree_query_source.name: memory_tree_query_source

query.description: Optional natural-language query for cosine-similarity rerank.

source_kind.description: Source kind filter when no exact id is known.

time_window_days.description: Only return summaries whose time range overlaps the last N days.

memory_tree_search_entities.description: Free-text LIKE search over the entity index — resolve a name or handle to a canonical id (e.g. "alice" -> `email:alice@example.com`). ALWAYS call this first when the user mentions someone by name before a `memory_tree` retrieval (`query_source` / `smart_walk` / `walk`) keyed on that id.
memory_tree_search_entities.name: memory_tree_search_entities

kinds.description: Optional kind filter — restrict to these entity kinds only.

memory_vector_search.description: Direct semantic vector search over memory chunks. Embeds the query and finds the most similar stored content by cosine similarity. Fast (single embedding call, no LLM). Use for semantic lookup when you know roughly what you're looking for. Returns chunk-level results with scores.
memory_vector_search.name: memory_vector_search

diverse.description: Apply MMR diversity to reduce redundancy among results (default false).

query.description: Natural-language query to embed and search against stored memory chunks.

source_kind.description: Filter to a specific source type.

time_window_days.description: Only include chunks from the last N days.
